contentBlocks.text: Systems of equations solve a genuinely common real-world question: at what point do two different pricing plans cost the same amount?

Phone Plan A costs $20 per month plus $0.10 per text. Phone Plan B costs $10 per month plus $0.15 per text. Set up two equations: y = 0.10x + 20 (Plan A) and y = 0.15x + 10 (Plan B), where x is number of texts and y is total cost. Since both equal y, set them equal: 0.10x + 20 = 0.15x + 10. Solve for x to find the 'break-even' number of texts where both plans cost the same, then find y (the cost at that point).
You just used a system of equations to find a genuine break-even point between two pricing plans. Tomorrow we'll review everything about systems of equations from this whole week.

objectives: Set up a system of equations from a real-world pricing scenario
Solve for and interpret a break-even point
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's three solving methods.
2. Work through the phone-plan example together, setting up both equations before solving.
3. Discuss what the break-even point actually means (fewer texts = Plan B cheaper, more texts = Plan A cheaper).
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide both equations already set up, and have the child focus only on solving the system
Ready for more: ask them which plan is better for someone who sends fewer than 200 texts, and which for someone who sends more
This is exactly how real subscription/pricing comparisons work — connect it to something the child has actually seen (phone plans, streaming services)
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Setting 0.10x+20 = 0.15x+10 gives 0.05x=10, so x=200 texts. 2. At x=200, cost = 0.10(200)+20 = $40. 3. Below 200 texts, Plan B is cheaper; above 200 texts, Plan A is cheaper.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Algebra 1 standard A-CED.3/A-REI.6: applying systems of linear equations to model and solve real-world problems, a genuine culmination of the week's three solving methods.

generationData.instructions: Plan A: y = 0.10x + 20. Plan B: y = 0.15x + 10. Solve each problem.

rows.problem: At how many texts (x) do both plans cost the same?
What is the total cost at that break-even point?
Which plan is cheaper for someone who sends fewer than 200 texts?
